_doc: Single approved set of numbers and wording (EVIDENCE_CONSISTENCY_SHEET.md, section C). status: approved | conditional | needs_confirmation. Not yet wired into build_ppt.py (PPT and video unchanged).

ram_peak.wording: Peak RAM while streaming: 245 KiB - under the 256 KB limit (final firmware; static 139.7 KB + peak heap 111.2 KB)

cpu_idle_both_cores_pct.wording: Idle CPU while listening, Wi-Fi connected: 5.5 % averaged over both cores (worst of our runs)

cpu_idle_busiest_core_pct.wording: Busiest core <= 9.5 % (8.6-9.5 % across runs; it rises with Wi-Fi traffic)

cpu_demo_build_pct.wording: The demo build also sends the microphone audio to the PC over USB (+~2 % CPU); the product firmware idles at 8.8 %

model.wording: 28 KB int8 model, 10.7 k parameters, 213 k MACs per inference, 13.4 KB tensor arena

cadence.wording: Every 10 ms a 40-band log-mel frame; the model scores the last 1 s every 60 ms

decision.wording: Detection when the mean of 3 scores >= 0.80; 2 s refractory

latency_keyword_end_to_server_ms.condition: final configuration: product firmware v2b + ASR server, 30 Sep, LAN, keyword with a pause
latency_keyword_end_to_server_ms.wording: Keyword end -> audio at the ASR server: 138 ms median, 196 ms p95 (final firmware, n = 12); about 110 ms of it is the on-device confirmation over 3 consecutive scores

latency_detection_to_first_audio_ms.wording: First audio reaches the ASR server 18 ms (median) after detection; 30 ms at p95 (final configuration)
latency_detection_to_first_audio_ms.note: 2 ms median without ASR load (E-37); 7-11 ms in other ASR sessions (E-62)

streaming.wording: Audio is sent only after a detection: from 571 ms before it until the end of speech, 16 kHz 16-bit (32 kB/s); streams arrive complete and bit-exact

no_clipping.wording: A command spoken straight after the keyword is inside the stream: it starts 571 ms before the detection, which comes <= 164 ms after the keyword ends (measured)

recall_speaker1.wording: Speaker 1, held-out session, 0.5-2 m: 22 of 25 keywords

recall_new_speaker.wording: New speaker never used in training: 20 of 25

false_triggers_quiet.wording: Quiet room: 1 false trigger in 5 h (held-out night)

false_triggers_tv.wording: Active household with TV/talk: 15.8 false triggers per hour - our main open issue

false_triggers_v4_comparison.wording: Retraining with the device's own false triggers cut this to 10.4 /h (v4) but lowered new-speaker recall to 14/25, so v2b ships

asr.wording: Server ASR: off-the-shelf Vosk en-in (publisher's WER 36 %); in the demo 3 of 4 commands were transcribed exactly

openness.wording: No proprietary voice SDK (checked on every build). The whole keyword pipeline is open source; the only closed code on the chip is Espressif's Wi-Fi/PHY radio driver and boot ROM, disclosed in the SBOM.

licence.wording: Our code is Apache-2.0. Two of the four TTS voices used for training are non-commercial, so commercial use needs retraining without them.

privacy.wording: Audio leaves the device only after a detection - true or false.

speakers.wording: Tested on 2 real speakers; trained with 4 TTS voices (US, UK, non-native English, Hindi) plus speaker 1

latency_keyword_end_to_server_earlier_ms.condition: 27 Sep, capture build, no ASR load - earlier configuration, not the headline

detection_t1.wording: 12 of 12 keywords detected on the final firmware, no extra triggers (1 speaker, n = 12)
